title: Constant field of a connected smooth affine scheme over a finite field
statement: Let k be a finite field and X a nonempty connected affine scheme smooth over k [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There is a finite field L equipped with a k-algebra structure [def-pc-field-extension] and a morphism g:X to Spec L factoring the given structure map through Spec L to Spec k. The morphism g is smooth and geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The underlying scheme X is unchanged.

proof.text: Smoothness makes X regular and connected regular X is integral. Write A for its global sections and let L be the actual integral closure of k in A. This is a field because A is a domain and k is a field. A finite point exists on the nonempty finite-type affine scheme; evaluation injects L into its finite residue field. Hence L is finite.

proof.text: The inclusion L into A defines g by the affine spectrum equivalence and factors the original structure morphism. Since the finite extension L/k is separable, it is etale. Formal smoothness of A over k lifts across the formally etale extension L/k; finite type over the Noetherian field L gives finite presentation. Thus g is smooth.

proof.text: The global sections of regular X are integrally closed. If an element of the function field is algebraic over L, transitivity makes it integral over k, hence over A. Integral closedness puts it in A and then in its integral closure L. Thus L is relatively algebraically closed in the function field. The field-extension criterion makes the generic-point scheme geometrically irreducible, hence geometrically connected. Its canonical map into connected X is over L, so the connected-image criterion proves that g is geometrically connected.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_geometricallyConnected_constant_field
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [Finite k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine X] [ConnectedSpace X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [Smooth f] :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Finite L) (_ : Algebra k L)
      (g : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)),
      f = g ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)) ∧
        Smooth g ∧ GeometricallyConnected g
